title: Client-stable operation identity and atomic server receipt
definition_of_done: Dart and server implementations reproduce the supplied canonical bytes and hashes. The operation ID is generated on the client before any server contact and is stable across retries, restarts and reconnects. The same ID and payload is idempotent success; an altered payload, UID or session under one ID produces a conflict that changes nothing. Server-minted IDs and tokens are receipts or mappings only and never block local acceptance.
estimate_basis: Pooled increment estimate in document 13; not an individual measured estimate

An altered payload or target under one ID produces a conflict." Active acceptance: FU-AC-095, FU-AC-097.

title: Terminal close versus late commit
definition_of_done: Race a send of the same operationId against itself, session closure and session deletion. Exactly one outcome per operation wins: COMMITTED, or a terminal refusal (class C3). The effect and its permanent fence entry commit in one transaction, and replay stays closed after detail receipt cleanup (ALREADY_COMMITTED_DETAIL_EXPIRED).
estimate_basis: Pooled increment estimate in document 13; not an individual measured estimate
amendment_note: EXTENDED by LOCAL_QUEUE_DECISION: replay, retention and terminal closure must hold for a command unacknowledged beyond the detailed-record TTL; a replay fence proves an old operation cannot apply again, not its historical outcome. See FU-AC-098, FU-AC-100. | REWRITTEN IN PLACE by LOCAL_QUEUE_DECISION (OFFLINE_COMMAND_PROTOCOL.md v1.3.1 sections 3.7, 4.4, 5). Old definition_of_done (withdrawn online admission model, not active): "Pause an effect past expiry and race it against terminal recovery and closure. Exactly one COMMITTED or CLOSED_NO_EFFECT result wins. Replay remains inadmissible after receipt cleanup."

The rest transition may start on local acceptance, but the UI never claims synced without a server acknowledgement. Cached plans, timers and unrelated manual paths still work. StartSet is not queued.
